\section{Left column start}
This fixture exercises a standard two-column article layout with sequential
paragraphs in each column. The left column must fill before body text wraps
into the right column, so layout recovery can observe a real gutter rather
than a single narrow stack of leftover lines.

Synthetic recovery notes occupy the remainder of the opening column. Column
clustering should keep these sentences together even when a heading sits
above a wrapped paragraph, and the gutter must stay empty of text. Repeated
prose is intentional: a short fixture never reaches the right column, which
made the previous two-column benchmark assert a single-column page.

Additional filler continues with layout-invariant language so the compiled
PDF remains deterministic. Band detection may fragment display gaps into
several strips; each strip of the body still has two columns once the left
column is full. The recovery pipeline should infer column boundaries and
reading order without relying on a naive sort-by-y-then-x heuristic alone.

Left column continues with enough text to wrap within the column width.
Paragraphs remain ordinary scholarly prose without tables, figures, or
display mathematics, so the only structural signal is the two-column
geometry itself.

A final left-column paragraph repeats the recovery contract: regions in the
left column are read top to bottom before any right-column region. If this
paragraph still sits in the left column, the following section heading
belongs to the right column in visual order.

One more left-column block of synthetic notes describes confidence, gutter
width, and unbalanced columns. Unbalanced columns must keep left-column
items together even when the right column continues further down the page.

\section{Right column body}
Right column material appears after the left column block in source order
when using the default \texttt{twocolumn} flow. This paragraph is the first
body block that must occupy the right column once the left column is full.

Further right-column sentences keep the second column from collapsing into
a narrow island. The benchmark asserts a MULTI\_COLUMN band on this page
and a reading order that visits left-column headings before this section.
